:football: *Week 9 Recap: 0.24 Points, One Bench Disaster, Zero Mercy*
_"Somewhere this week, a quarter of a point decided a marriage-ending argument. We'll get there."_

:heart-8bit: *League Pulse*
The Blackberries and Penalty Flag Sachin played ninety-plus minutes of fantasy football to settle it by 0.24 points — the kind of margin that makes you double-check the box score, then triple-check it, then accept that the universe is simply cruel. Everywhere else, the standings did what standings do: the top stayed top, the bottom kept finding new ways to lose, and one manager left 79 points of talent on the bench like it was a customer satisfaction survey nobody asked for.

:confused-math-lady: *Stat of the Week*
<@U09KVP9JHQS>'s Goal Line Stand Jesse left 79.28 points on the bench this week and still only lost by 3.94. Retention strategy: retaining last place.

:footballl: *Matchups*

*<@U08SKVCGDQW>'s The Blackberries (95.8) def. <@U0761N3RYSW>'s Penalty Flag Sachin (95.56)*
_Decided By A Rounding Error_

The Blackberries survived despite benching Corey Kiner's 11.5 points twice over, which should have been a problem and somehow wasn't. Sachin's real sin: starting DeMario Douglas (15.2, 19.9% started) over a shelved Rome Odunze (16.0, 56.2% started) — the consensus pick, sitting right there. Combined score: 191.4. Margin: 0.24. A/B tested a bench swap. Both variants barely mattered.

*<@U03FE7P8EEP>'s Purdy Boys (100.62) def. <@U09KVP9JHQS>'s Goal Line Stand Jesse (96.68)*
_Why?_

Jesse benched Matthew Golden, 86.7% started leaguewide, who dropped 32.4 points from the pine, in favor of DJ Moore's 6.6. That's a 25.8-point unforced error, and it still wasn't the only one; Jordan Love logged 36.2 points doing nothing. Purdy Boys didn't need to be great. They needed Jesse to keep doing this, and Jesse delivered.

*<@U08SD0PJ3EU>'s big d's fantasy (95.78) def. <@U03R72JAKFH>'s Morgan's Team! (89.1)*
_The Quiet One_

Morgan's Team! got a respectable floor from Jonah Coleman (18.8) and still fell short by 6.68. Danielle's crew converted a middling lineup into a win — no heroics, no disasters, just a churn-rate win nobody will remember by Thursday.

*<@U0405KM3X7C>'s Hut Hut Eich (105.52) def. <@U03L8KFL1RS>'s Monster of the Midway (82.44)*
_Narrator: The Bench Would, In Fact, Outscore The Starters_

Monster of the Midway's best performer this week never left the bench: C.J. Stroud put up 36.4 there (our Bench Hero of the Week, for what that's worth), though at 30.5% started leaguewide, that was a defensible sit. The real crime was benching Denzel Boston's 15.8 for a zeroed-out Garrett Wilson. That's 15.8 points surrendered to vibes. Hut Hut Eich collected the 23-point win regardless.

*<@U032LD8RMK8>'s Scott’s Tots (123.34) def. <@U08QHPYDZ46>'s Dasher Mafia (92.4)*
_Seven Straight, One Near-Miss_

Scott's Tots rode Joe Burrow's 29.5 to a seventh straight win, then nearly tripped over their own kicker — benching Cam Little's 17.0 for Eddy Pineiro's 8.0, a 9-point donation at the one position where it should never happen. Dasher Mafia's bench outscored its DEF slot by a wide margin and it still wasn't enough. Conversion funnel working perfectly: converting a laugher into a formality.

*<@U0AV2EB5GUD>'s Game of Throws (134.06) def. <@U02C39SFXPD>'s Stiff Arm tim (91.82)*
_The QB Swap That Didn't Need To Happen_

Kenneth Walker III's 36.3 did the heavy lifting for Game of Throws, who barely had to manage anything right. Stiff Arm tim, meanwhile, started Justin Herbert (11.4, 12.2% started) over a benched Bryce Young (21.3, 23.3% started) — a 9.9-point gap at the one position with no excuse. Churn rate: 100% of this week's playoff math.

*<@UPQ8CPJDR>'s High Quality TD Rate (175.18) def. <@U07JPH677ED>'s Blitz Squad Joseph (100.68)*
_The Blowout of the Week, Technically Speaking_

High Quality TD Rate posted 175.18, with Puka Nacua alone good for 35.0 of it, and buried Blitz Squad Joseph by 74.5. The twist: Joseph left only 2.0 points on the bench, our Coach of the Week by a mile. Perfect lineup management. Still lost by three touchdowns and change. Sometimes the customer journey ends at the unsubscribe button no matter how good your onboarding was.

3. <@U08SKVCGDQW> (6-3, PF 1072.3) :triangle_downred: 1 — won by 0.24 and will take it over losing by 40

:disappointed-guy: *Fourth and Long: Week 10 Preview*
• Game of the Week: <@U08SKVCGDQW>'s The Blackberries (6-3) vs <@UPQ8CPJDR>'s High Quality TD Rate (8-1) — the league's hottest team meets the team that just won by a quarter-point. Something has to give.
• Trap Game: <@U0405KM3X7C>'s Hut Hut Eich (5-4) vs <@U0761N3RYSW>'s Penalty Flag Sachin (5-4) — identical records, opposite momentum. Easy to overlook, dangerous to sleep on.
• One-liner forecast: <@U03L8KFL1RS>'s Monster of the Midway (3-6, six straight losses) hosts <@U02C39SFXPD>'s Stiff Arm tim (3-6) in a battle neither team's bench seems to want them to win.

:person_in_lotus_position: *Closing Thoughts*
_"Next week's disasters are already loading. See you then."_

:football: *Week 10 Recap: 3.82 Points and a Bench Full of Regret*
_"3.82 points isn't a margin. It's a dare."_

:heart-8bit: *League Pulse*
Open on the nail-biter: <@U0761N3RYSW>'s Penalty Flag Sachin needed every one of its 107.64 points to hold off <@U0405KM3X7C>'s Hut Hut Eich, 103.82, a 3.82-point margin that should have gone the other way given what Sachin left sitting on the bench. Up top, the race stayed a two-team affair at 8-2, though <@UPQ8CPJDR>'s High Quality TD Rate finally took an L after weeks of untouchable point totals. Down in the basement, three teams are now welded to 3-7, and the only thing separating them is churn rate.

:confused-math-lady: *Stat of the Week*
<@U03FE7P8EEP>'s Purdy Boys left 78.76 points on the bench this week — more than Dasher Mafia (69.08) or Stiff Arm tim (73.3) scored in their entire games, and it still didn't cost them the win.

:footballl: *Matchups*

*<@U0761N3RYSW>'s Penalty Flag Sachin (107.64) def. <@U0405KM3X7C>'s Hut Hut Eich (103.82)*
_Nearly Self-Destructed, Won Anyway_

Sachin benched George Pickens, 43.5 points and this week's Bench Hero at 83.1% started leaguewide, for a DeMario Douglas who scored 1.4 — a 56.7-point management gap on the week, and it still barely held up. Hut Hut Eich played a flawless lineup, zero points left anywhere, and still lost by 3.82. A perfect process, an imperfect outcome. Welcome to fantasy football.

*<@U03L8KFL1RS>'s Monster of the Midway (105.24) def. <@U02C39SFXPD>'s Stiff Arm tim (73.3)*
_Why Bench a Tight End Who Outscores Your Tight End by 14.7?_

Ja'Marr Chase went off for 34.1 and it barely mattered, because Stiff Arm tim started Darnell Washington (1.5) over a benched Mark Andrews (16.2) at the same position — a 28.6-point gap, flagged roastable for a reason. Monster of the Midway didn't need to be sharp; C.J. Stroud's 21.4 and two solid backs were enough to snap back into the win column.

*<@U07JPH677ED>'s Blitz Squad Joseph (154.5) def. <@U09KVP9JHQS>'s Goal Line Stand Jesse (121.18)*
_The Shootout_

Combined score: 275.68, this week's Shootout of the Week, and Christian McCaffrey's 46.3 made sure Joseph's side won it outright. Jesse's lineup wasn't the problem this time, a tidy 5.7-point management gap with nothing roastable in it — he just ran into a buzzsaw. Trevor Lawrence's 27.8 was a customer acquisition win in a quarter nobody else noticed.

*<@U08SKVCGDQW>'s The Blackberries (133.42) def. <@UPQ8CPJDR>'s High Quality TD Rate (97.12)*
_The League's Best Offense Went Quiet_

Dak Prescott's 35.4 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 31.1 did the heavy lifting for a Blackberries squad that left zero points unused — perfect lineup, fourth straight win. High Quality TD Rate got 35.4 from Patrick Mahomes and nothing from anyone else worth mentioning; the league's highest point total all season just took an L, 36.3 points clear of comfortable.

*<@U03FE7P8EEP>'s Purdy Boys (132.46) def. <@U03R72JAKFH>'s Morgan's Team! (94.9)*
_A Flex Spot Worth 35 Points_

Emmett Johnson's 35.1 out of the flex slot carried Purdy Boys to a second straight win, with enough margin that the 78.76 points gathering dust on the bench never came into play. Morgan's Team! actually ran a clinic on roster management, Coach of the Week honors and zero points wasted — and still lost by 37.56. Conversion funnel working perfectly for everyone except the team doing everything right.

*<@U032LD8RMK8>'s Scott’s Tots (146.56) def. <@U0AV2EB5GUD>'s Game of Throws (82.42)*
_Drake Maye's Day Off_

Jahmyr Gibbs turned in 44.2 points by himself, pushing Scott’s Tots to an eighth straight win and the league's hottest streak by a mile. Game of Throws never had a chance once Drake Maye logged 3.0 points at quarterback — not a bench decision, just a quarterback torching his own trade value live on the box score. Isaiah Likely's 27.7 was the only thing resembling offense.

*<@U08SD0PJ3EU>'s big d's fantasy (135.56) def. <@U08QHPYDZ46>'s Dasher Mafia (69.08)*
_The Blowout of the Week, Self-Inflicted_

big d's fantasy ran a perfect lineup, Brock Purdy's 31.7 and a 20-point game from the Vikings defense, zero waste anywhere — for this week's biggest margin, 66.48. Dasher Mafia helped out: Jared Goff sat on the bench with 22.4 points, 55.4% owned leaguewide, while Tyler Shough started and managed 11.0. An A/B test with an obvious control group, run anyway, retention of last place basically guaranteed.

:disappointed-guy: *Fourth and Long: Week 11 Preview*
• Game of the Week: <@U0405KM3X7C>'s Hut Hut Eich (5-5) vs <@UPQ8CPJDR>'s High Quality TD Rate (8-2) — a team that played a perfect lineup and still lost meets the league's highest scorer fresh off a rare stumble.
• Trap Game: <@U0AV2EB5GUD>'s Game of Throws (4-6) vs <@U08SD0PJ3EU>'s big d's fantasy (4-6) — big d's just authored a 66-point blowout and may be feeling generous; Game of Throws just absorbed the second-biggest margin of the week and has nowhere left to go but up.
• One-liner forecast: <@U03R72JAKFH>'s Morgan's Team! (3-7) hosts <@U08QHPYDZ46>'s Dasher Mafia (3-7) in a game that will not be remembered by either side.
